key_insight: A real-time vision pipeline can detect resistance spot weld defects and predict maintenance needs directly on an automotive assembly line.
engineering_relevance: This enables earlier intervention on failing robots and weld points, improving quality control, uptime, and maintenance prioritization in robotic welding cells.
method: YOLOv8 detects spot welds and extracts physical features such as nugget diameter and heat-affected zone.
A neural network with linear discriminant analysis classifies defective welds.
A CNN predicts maintenance category: maintenance-free, predictive, preventive, or corrective.
evidence_signal: Trained on images from 674 cabins collected over 30 continuous hours, the system achieved 95.80% accuracy for defect classification and 94.72% precision for maintenance prediction.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on a specific automotive line, so robustness to different weld geometries, lighting conditions, and production settings still needs validation.
paper_title: An AI-Based Vision System for Detecting Defects in Resistance Spot Welding and Predicting Maintenance in Robotic Cells
